decisive_items: There were confluent erythematous, edematous plaques in the bilateral periorbital areas (left more than right), studded with numerous 2– to 3-mm pustules, some coalescing into “lakes of pus.”
A few pustules were also noted in the perioral area
She had been applying this ointment to her face at least daily for 2 years, pausing for no more than 1–2 days at a time because the rash promptly returned
response.rationale: Periorificial pustular plaques with “lakes of pus” and prolonged topical corticosteroid use point to perioral dermatitis; R1’s steroid-induced rosacea-like label is close but less directly anchored by the specific morphology and absence of atrophy/telangiectasia.

rejected.why: Shares the steroid mechanism, but the rosacea-like qualifier is less directly supported and the absence of steroid-induced atrophy/telangiectasia weakens it.
No culprit contact allergen; contact dermatitis would not explain the periorificial pustular eruption with lakes of pus.
Topical steroid withdrawal is a mechanism rather than the specific dermatosis; the perioral/periorbital pustular morphology is characteristic of perioral dermatitis.
